question.leadin: The Battle of Inchon was a major offensive in this conflict, and this war ended with the establishment of the Demilitarized Zone at the 38th Parallel.
question.text: Name this conflict that ended with an armistice dividing a namesake peninsula.
question.answerHtml: Korean War [accept “Conflict” in place of “War;” or Hanguk Jeonjaeng; or Choguk haebang chonjaeng]
question.clue: The Armistice Agreement that ended this war was signed shortly after Joseph Stalin's death caused a withdrawal of Soviet support.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Asian political families.
swap.text: One member of this country's Kim family was ostracized after trying to visit Tokyo Disneyland and was mysteriously assassinated in 2017.
swap.answerHtml: <u>North Korea</u> (or <u>Democratic People’s Republic of Korea</u>; or <u>DPRK</u>; do not accept or prompt on Republic of Korea)
swap.clue: This country diverged from traditional Marxism-Leninism with its Juche ideology.

question.leadin: After conducting "literati purges" against members of the Sarim faction, one emperor banned an alphabet used in this peninsula to suppress criticism of his regime.
question.text: Name this East Asian peninsula, once home to the kingdom of Joseon ["JOH-sun"]. This peninsula juts off of modern-day Russia and China and is separated from Japan by a namesake strait.
question.clue: A military commander employed by a kingdom in this region designed so-called "turtle ships" to counter the forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi; that commander was Yi Sun-Sin.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about yellow ribbons in history.
swap.text: Victims of the Sewol ferry disaster in this country are commemorated with yellow ribbons. The Miracle on the Han River refers to massive growth in this country's capital of Seoul.
swap.answerHtml: South Korea [or the Republic of Korea; or ROK; prompt on Korea; reject “North Korea” or the “Democratic People’s Republic of Korea”]
swap.clue: This country's first female leader led it from 2013 until her 2017 impeachment.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the abolition of slavery throughout the world.
question.text: This dynasty abolished slavery in Korea as part of the Gabo Reforms in 1894. This dynasty declared Korea an empire in 1897; however, it would be annexed to the Japanese empire in 1910.
question.clue: This dynasty was destabilized by succession crises called the Strifes of the Princes.

swap.text: During the lead up to this time period, the forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei used fire ships to turn back the much larger force of Cao Cao at the Battle of Red Cliffs. This time period followed the collapse of the Han dynasty.
swap.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

question.text: During the Korean War, Douglas MacArthur planned and executed this naval landing, allowing UN forces to break out of the Pusan perimeter.
question.answerHtml: Battle of Inch (e)on [accept Incheon Sangnyuk Jakjeon; accept Operation Chromite]

swap.text: This dynasty during the Three Kingdoms Period divided its people into "true bone" and "sacred bone," and it was founded by Hyeokgeose. The people of this dynasty later conquered the Goguryeo and Baekje empires.
swap.clue: This dynasty employed a cultured class of cosmetic-using soldiers called the "flowering knights," or "hwarang."

question.text: This fourth emperor of the Joseon dynasty is credited with developing the phonetic Hangul writing system in the 1400s, though yangban elites resisted the change.
question.clue: It was said that an innovation from this monarch's reign could be learnt by wise men in a morning and by stupid men in ten days.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the history of Buddhism in Korea.
swap.text: Warrior monks in the Righteous Army were active participants in the first of these events. After a brief exile, Admiral Yi Sun-shin led his forces to victory in the Battle of Myeongnyang (myung-n'YAHNG) during one of these events.
swap.answerHtml: Japanese invasions of Korea [or Toyotomi Hideyoshi's invasions of the Korean peninsula; or Imjin War; or Wanil Korean Campaign; or Bunroku no ek; or Keichō no eki; or Kara iri]
swap.clue: That one of these events eventually ended at the Battle of Noryang.

question.leadin: This kingdom's ruler Gwanggaeto the Great erected a massive stele on the banks of the Yalu River detailing its history.
question.text: Name this northernmost of Korea's Three Kingdoms, which repelled an invading Sui Dynasty army of more than 300,000 soldiers by drowning almost all of them at the Battle of the Salsu River.
question.clue: Some of the best-preserved art of this kingdom survives in the tomb of Dong Shou at a complex at Anak.

swap.leadin: This kinship system was weakened by the 1746 Dress act, which prohibited wearing kilts or identifying patterns.
swap.text: What name is given to these family and extended groups identified by their differing tartans?
swap.clue: What are these kinship groups in which members often took the chief's surname and which often have a distinctive tartan pattern?

question.text: The Joson dynasty was preceded by this kingdom which was formed by the union of the earlier Three Kingdoms. Its king Gongmin managed to break free of Mongol control, but was unable to stop the dynasty's decline and eventual end in the late 14th century.
question.clue: Monarchs of this kingdom like its Kwangjong had the surname Wang, including its founder, Wang Geon ("gun").

swap.leadin: In 1866, France occupied this island for six weeks following the execution of seven Catholic missionaries during a crackdown on Christians initiated by Heungseon Daewongun.
swap.text: Name this island, where the Japanese ship Un'yo provoked a battle that led to an 1876 unequal treaty named for it. That treaty named for this island ended the Joseon Kingdom's status as a tributary of the Qing Dynasty.

question.leadin: This kingdom is traditionally said to have been founded by Hyokkose.
question.text: Name this kingdom that unified a peninsula after conquering neighboring Paekche and Koguryo with the help of the Tang Dynasty, then expelled Tang forces.
question.clue: This kingdom included the hereditary "head rank 6" caste in its "bone rank" system, and used highly-educated elite knights whose name means "flower boys."

swap.text: In the initial phase of the war, North Korean forces pushed UN troops back to this feature, named for a very southern Korean city. The so-called "Bowling Alley" was one segment of this feature.

question.leadin: Identify the following about Korean history FTPE.
question.text: This first native Korean state arose near the Yalu River in the first century CE and conquered the Chinese colony of Lolang.
question.clue: Under Yang, China attempted to conquer this kingdom, which opposed Baekje and Silla during the Korean Three Kingdoms Period. That invasion failed after the Battle of the Salsu River.

swap.leadin: This man's wife is called "Ri Sol-ju," though it is almost certainly a pseudonym, and many believe that she is actually a singer and that the government is destroying evidence of her past identity.
swap.text: Name this Supreme Leader of North Korea.
swap.clue: He was involved in a naval shelling of a contested island and continued the internment camps begun under this man's predecessor.

question.leadin: He declared his namesake "line" in a 1952 speech in order to protect his country's interests in the Sea of Japan, including fishing rights around the Liaodong Rocks. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this man who died in exile in Hawaii, the first president of the Republic of South Korea.
question.clue: Protests against him began after a fisherman discovered the dead body of a high schooler with a tear gas capsule lodged in his eye near the port city of Masan.

swap.leadin: It began when Wang Kon united the kingdoms of Goguryeo, Silla and Baekje.
swap.text: Name this Korean dynasty that reigned from 918 to 1392.
swap.clue: Twenty-nine women from hojeok ("HO-juck") families were married to this dynasty's founder, Wang Geon ("gun").
